lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Eating the Right Amounts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about healthy eating from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about healthy eating.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about eating the right amounts of different foods.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Why do we need a balanced diet?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about healthy eating.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about healthy eating at home.

lessons.title: Food Survey: Block Diagram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a block diagram of a food survey.
success_criteria: I can build a block diagram.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a survey of favourite healthy foods, representing in a block diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct and represent a food survey, answering questions about it.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation applied to a health context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple food survey with your family.

lessons.title: What Makes a Balanced Diet?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a balanced diet includes.
success_criteria: I can name a food group.
I can say why we need it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss different foods eaten in a typical day.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce food groups (fruit/veg, carbohydrates, protein, dairy) and why a balanced diet is important.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort food picture cards into food groups, recording reasoning.
key_questions: What food group is this in?
Why do we need this food group?

differentiation.greater_depth: Sort all food groups and explain their importance

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of balanced diet, a Year 2 objective — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the food groups in your dinner tonight.

lessons.title: Writing a Healthy Meal Plan
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a description of a healthy meal using varied vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can describe a healthy meal.
I can name foods from different groups.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a description of a healthy, balanced meal.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a description of their own healthy meal plan.

differentiation.greater_depth: Write a detailed plan including multiple food groups

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing applied to health knowledge — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share healthy meal plans with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Plan a healthy meal with your family.

lessons.title: Exercise Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using an exercise context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using an exercise context (e.g. laps run, star jumps done).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve exercise-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up an exercise word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Why Is Exercise Important?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why exercise is important for the body.
success_criteria: I can name a benefit of exercise.
I can name a type of exercise.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why exercise is important (strong heart, muscles, releases energy, feeling good).
lessons.independent_task: Children record benefits of exercise and their favourite way to exercise.
key_questions: Why is exercise good for us?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain benefits in more scientific detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of exercise importance, a Year 2 objective — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Do a favourite exercise with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Healthy Living Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read healthy-living-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read healthy living words.
I can read a sentence about healthy living.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to healthy-living-themed words (e.g. 'fruit', 'exercise', 'sleep').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading healthy living words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Exercise: Distance and Time
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure distance and time during a simple exercise activity.
success_criteria: I can measure a distance.
I can time an activity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap measuring distance and telling the time.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring a running/jumping distance and timing an activity.
lessons.independent_task: Children take part in a simple exercise activity, measuring distance/time and recording results.

differentiation.greater_depth: Record and compare results across multiple attempts

lessons.assessment_notes: Note practical application of measuring skills to a PE/science crossover — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Time or measure an exercise activity at home.

lessons.title: Exercise and Our Heart Rate
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe how exercise affects heart rate simply.
success_criteria: I can feel my heart beating faster after exercise.
I can say why this happens.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel resting heart rate/pulse (simply, placing hand on chest).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that exercise makes the heart beat faster to pump blood/oxygen around the body.
lessons.independent_task: Children do a short burst of exercise, then observe and describe how their heart/breathing feels different.
resources_needed: Open space for a short exercise burst
key_questions: How does your heart feel now?

differentiation.support: Adult supports observation and simple description
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the reason for heart rate change in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observation of a bodily response to exercise — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap how exercise affects the heart.
lessons.home_link: Notice how your heart feels after playing actively at home.

lessons.title: Healthy Habits Discussion
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss and justify healthy habit choices.
success_criteria: I can name a healthy habit.
I can explain why it's good for me.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap healthy eating and exercise learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model discussing a healthy habit with justification.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record a healthy habit they have or would like to build, with reasoning.
key_questions: What healthy habit do you have?
Why is it good for you?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the benefit in scientific detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and application of health knowledge — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Try a healthy habit with your family this week.

lessons.title: Fractions: Balanced Plate
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use fractions to represent a balanced plate of food.
success_criteria: I can divide a plate into fractions.
I can say what food goes in each part.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model dividing a plate diagram into fractions to represent balanced proportions of food groups.
lessons.independent_task: Children design a balanced plate using fractions to show food group proportions.
key_questions: What fraction is fruit and veg?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use thirds, quarters and halves accurately

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to a real-world health context — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Look at a real meal and estimate its food group fractions.

lessons.title: Planning a Healthy Day
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plan a day including healthy eating, exercise, and rest.
success_criteria: I can include a healthy meal.
I can include exercise and rest.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all healthy living learning this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss planning a balanced day including food, exercise, and rest/sleep.
lessons.independent_task: Children plan a healthy day, including meals, exercise, and rest.
key_questions: What healthy choices will you include?
Have you balanced activity and rest?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's healthy living learning — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Try following your healthy day plan.

lessons.title: Healthy Eating and Exercise Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about healthy eating and exercise.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's healthy living learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about healthy eating and exercise, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why do we need a balanced diet?
Why might exercise help us sleep better?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on healthy eating and exercise facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Data, Fractions, Measuring
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply data, fraction and measuring skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read a block diagram.
I can find fractions of a plate.
I can measure distance/time.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's data, fraction, and measuring learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: What does the block diagram show?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 22 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.STAT/N4/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising fractions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Healthy Eating and Exercise Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about healthy eating and exercise.
success_criteria: I can name a food group and why it matters.
I can name a benefit of exercise.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering food groups, balanced diets, and exercise benefits.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Healthy Eating and Exercise' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about healthy eating and exercise?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note healthy living understanding progress, setting up hygiene next week — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's healthy eating and exercise learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about healthy living with your family.
